ctor.rationale: `base(3, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (RollingBoulder.cs:23-26) == cost 3 / POWER / RARE / SELF.

CanonicalVars.maps_to: _power_amount = 5 declared; the IncrementAmount var is not (colorless_powers.py:305)
CanonicalVars.issue: `new PowerVar<RollingBoulderPower>(5m)` maps to `_power_amount = 5`, but the second var `new DynamicVar("IncrementAmount", 5m)` (RollingBoulder.cs:17-21, mirrored by the `public const int incrementAmount = 5`) has no `_`-attribute -- the sim leaves the per-turn growth entirely to RollingBoulderPower. The APPLIED amount is right and the power's growth is the power stream's to audit; what is missing is the printed second number, so `magic_number` reports the starting 5 and nothing tells the observation encoder that it grows. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bad_luck's CanonicalVars entry (rule 3): a printed number the sim's `magic_number` cannot surface, so `full_env.card_features` (full_env.py:455-489) encodes the card without it. DORMANT for game fidelity, LIVE for the observation encoder.

OnPlay.rationale: `PowerCmd.Apply<RollingBoulderPower>(choiceContext, Owner.Creature, DynamicVars["RollingBoulderPower"].IntValue, Owner.Creature, this)` (RollingBoulder.cs:30) == `PowerCmd.apply(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, RollingBoulderPower, self._power_amount, applier=ctx.player)`. No animation on either side.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars["RollingBoulderPower"].UpgradeValueBy(5m)` (RollingBoulder.cs:35) == `self._power_amount += 5` (5 -> 10). The IncrementAmount stays 5 when upgraded -- only the STARTING damage doubles, which is the distinction the missing var would have made visible.
